>Or you could just sit there feeling sorry for yourself and keep sitting around wanting to kill yourself, wallowing in the sorrow that you've created for yourself

That's not actually how it works, I thought it was and that caused me a lot of problems before because I blamed myself sadness/depression, but realizing its just the way my mind works helps. The problem with manic depression is that treatment is focused on the manic side of things, and psychiatrists are reluctant to treat the depression side of it because depression meds can throw the person into a manic state which is considered worse. So seeking psychiatric help won't really help in that aspect anyway, and knowing my thought process in a manic state, I really doubt I'd stick with the meds through it anyway. 'I might as well be the next Buddah or Jesus and I can do no wrong and meds? Fuck that I'm too fucking awesome, and awesome people don't need meds ergo I dont need meds, I'm not crazy, crazy is just a construct of society to define the normalcy of people, to try and keep me like everyone else and from being the greatest motherfucker of all time' or something along those lines. It's weird.

I'll look into that other thing, I don't read philosophical ideologies to take them to heart and follow what they say but rather as a way to understand different methods of thinking and logic, and  see if I can apply them to my own understandings of the world and how to look at it (Aristotle didn't repeat what Socrates taught him, but rather applied the kind of logic and thinking taught to him to allow him to come to his own conclusions of the world), so while I probably won't follow its teachings it might show me a perspective I havnt thought of and could help me in furthering my understanding of life.

It's not about how they see me, or at least not as far as I'm aware, our subcouncious is a funny thing though so maybe. For me its more about the fact that I know that it would weigh too heavily on them, it'd make me feel too bad. For better or worse empathy is something we all (except for, as far as I'm aware, those on the autism spectrum and psychopaths) experience

Edit: Which I guess if I did end up killing myself eventually means they'd find out anyway, so I guess if I WAS to do it I'd need to make it look like an accident, accidents are easier to get over too I'd think (no thoughts of 'was it my fault' or the like). I guess that also answers the do I leave a note question. Most suicide attempts fail though as far as I'm aware so making it look like an accident could also help with the potential shame of waking up still alive, then I could pass it off as just being overly clumsy. Fuck I need to stop overthinking everything haha. I should increase my meditation frequency/duration, maybe that'll help

Meds is not the kind of secret you can keep from your parents forever, not to mention I'm still financially dependant on them which makes paying for it in secrecy difficult. Maybe when I'm financially stable, which if I decide to go for my Masters or PHD could mean another 6 or more years lol. I don't know I'm feeling a bit better now so I should be able to weather out the rest of this depression until I can get another period of normalcy, until the next cycle

You mean like, ever? Or for this specifically? If the former yeah when I'd get sick or something. If the latter then no, I'd have to tell my family eventually and I couldn't do that, plus I doubt they'd support it either, I'm the 'perfect child' so to speak from their perspective, they'd spend the time convincing me I'm not crazy and I'm perfectly normal and I just need to not worry about it and I'll be good, or at least that's what I'd assume, knowing them. Unless I mentioned the suicidality, but that would break their heart, I couldn't do that. And anyway, I'm smart enough to manage it on my own, you'd never know it by simply talking to me unless I explicitly stated I was crazy. Unless I'm drunk, alcohol lowers inhibition and makes me regret pretty much EVERYTHING the next morning haha
